newsitem.title: GERMANY: BMW to invest 600 mln sterling in Rover.
newsitem.headline: BMW to invest 600 mln sterling in Rover.

text.p: Bayerische Motoren Werke AG (BMW) Chief Financial Officer Volker Doppelfeld said on Tuesday that the company would invest 600 million pounds ($969.6 million) sterling in its British unit Rover Group this year.
BMW, which purchased Rover in 1994, invested 1.2 billion marks in Rover last year as part of a multi-year plan to improve efficiency at the company and make it profitable by 2000.
According to German accounting standards, Rover posted a 279 million mark pre-tax loss on ordinary business activities in 1996, down from a 335 million mark loss the year before.
Worldwide sales of Rover Group cars increased five percent last year to more than 507,000 units.
Doppelfeld said 1996 deliveries of the Rover 200 model were hurt by a model change-over, but those of the Rover 400, introduced in 1995, grew by two-thirds to 127,900 units.
Deliveries of Land Rover's off-road vehicles, thought the most profitable part of the Rover group, rose eight percent last year to 125,200 units.
Doppelfeld said BMW is sticking to its plan of investing in the group an amount about equal to seven to eight percent of sales.
